proposals.before: In the eighth year of the Yongzheng reign he was promoted to prefect of Qinzhou and served concurrently as acting prefect of Lu'an.
proposals.after: In the eighth year of the Yongzheng reign he was promoted to department magistrate (zhizhou) of Qinzhou and served as acting prefect of Lu'an.
proposals.reason: 知州 is the department magistrate, not prefect; only 署潞安知府 is an acting prefecture post. The idiomatic English fuses both as prefect.

proposals.before: In the eighth year of Yongzheng he was promoted to prefect of Qinzhou and acted as prefect of Lu'an.
proposals.after: In the eighth year of Yongzheng he was promoted to department magistrate of Qinzhou and acted as prefect of Lu'an.
proposals.reason: The literal English likewise renders 沁州知州 as prefect, colliding with the distinct 知府 office of Lu'an.

proposals.before: At the time a rumor spread that sorcerers were cutting people's hair; Xiaoshan arrested the monks Liaofan and three others, who confessed under false coercion, and Mengshuo reversed the verdict.
proposals.after: At the time a rumor spread that sorcerers were cutting people's hair; Xiaoshan arrested the monk Liaofan and three others, who confessed under false coercion, and Mengshuo reversed the verdict.
proposals.reason: 僧了凡等四人 names one monk plus three others; the literal 'monks Liaofan and three others' wrongly makes all four monks.

proposals.before: Jie Xi, whose courtesy name was Dingbu, came from Jiezhou in Shanxi.
proposals.after: Jie Xizhou, whose courtesy name was Dingbu, came from Jiezhou in Shanxi.
proposals.reason: The personal name 介錫週 includes 週; rendering it as Jie Xi drops the given-name's second character.

proposals.before: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Pingyuan.
proposals.after: He was transferred to serve as department magistrate of Pingyuan.
proposals.reason: 知州 is a department (zhou) magistracy, not a prefecture (知府).

proposals.before: He was transferred to be prefect of Pingyuan.
proposals.after: He was transferred to be department magistrate of Pingyuan.
proposals.reason: 知州 is a department magistracy, not a prefecture (知府).

proposals.before: Wang Zuxian of Nanlong had always been a man of no fixed occupation.
proposals.after: Wang Zuxian of Nanlong had always been without household registration.
proposals.reason: 無籍 refers to lacking official registration (籍), not merely lacking an occupation; the literal field already has the registration sense.

proposals.before: Xi was ordered to join in the joint investigation. Finding the charges groundless throughout, he released Wenjia and all those implicated with him. Fugitives returned from hiding, and the border was pacified.
proposals.after: Xi was ordered to join in the joint investigation. He determined guilt and innocence justly throughout, released Wenjia and all those implicated with him. Fugitives returned from hiding, and the border was pacified.
proposals.reason: 蔽罪悉當 means the determinations of guilt were all appropriate, not that the charges were groundless throughout; release of Wenjia follows from just adjudication.

proposals.before: Xi received orders to go and jointly try the cases; the charges under examination were all valid; he released Wenjia and those implicated with him; the fugitives all returned, and the borderland was pacified.
proposals.after: Xi received orders to go and jointly try the cases; the determinations of guilt were all appropriate; he released Wenjia and those implicated with him; the fugitives all returned, and the borderland was pacified.
proposals.reason: 蔽罪悉當 means the judgments were fitting, not that the charges were valid; release of the implicated follows from just adjudication.

proposals.before: In the eighth year of Yongzheng, After receiving his jinshi degree, he was promoted from vice director in the Ministry of Punishments to supervising censor of the Shandong circuit.
proposals.after: In the eighth year of Yongzheng, after receiving his jinshi degree, he was promoted from vice director in the Ministry of Punishments to supervising censor of the Shandong circuit.
proposals.reason: Mid-sentence capital After after a comma is a grammatical error, not an intended new sentence.

proposals.before: Sun Jiagao's integrity is beyond reproach and has long been known to the throne; yet to fine him and require him to pay for labor—governors-general and governors everywhere may conclude that even Jiagao's record cannot escape censure, that any slip will bring a fine,​​ and they will abandon integrity and budget for fines in advance.
proposals.after: Sun Jiagao's integrity is beyond reproach and has long been known to the throne; yet to fine him and require him to pay for labor—governors-general and governors everywhere may conclude that even Jiagao's record cannot escape censure, that any slip will bring a fine, and they will abandon integrity and budget for fines in advance.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English contains stray U+200B zero-width spaces after the comma, a corruption not present as wording in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Sun Jiagao's conduct is not lax, long within the sage ruler's penetrating scrutiny, yet to fine him and order him to contribute funds for service—fearing that governor-generals and governors throughout the realm will hear of it and say that with Jiagao's conduct he still cannot escape censure and fine, or that if once he is not correct, fines will follow in succession,​​ inevitably they will destroy integrity and prepare ground for accepting fines in advance.
proposals.after: Sun Jiagao's conduct is not lax, long within the sage ruler's penetrating scrutiny, yet to fine him and order him to contribute funds for service—fearing that governor-generals and governors throughout the realm will hear of it and say that with Jiagao's conduct he still cannot escape censure and fine, or that if once he is not correct, fines will follow in succession, inevitably they will destroy integrity and prepare ground for accepting fines in advance.
proposals.reason: The literal English likewise inserts stray U+200B characters after the comma.

proposals.before: When there are vagrant people and mineral earth, the commandant immediately heavily punishes the offenses of governor-generals, governors, and prefectural and county officials.
proposals.after: When there are vagrant people or wasteland, the authorities should immediately heavily punish the offenses of governors-general, governors, and prefectural and county officials.
proposals.reason: 礦土 is wasteland rather than mineral earth; 尉即 marks immediate injunction, not a commandant as the actor.

proposals.before: Fearing that entering summer epidemics would arise, he gave each mouth two months' grain and sent envoys to return them to plowing.
proposals.after: Fearing that epidemics would arise as summer began, he gave each person two months' grain and sent them home to return to plowing.
proposals.reason: 遣使歸耕 means he caused the refugees to go back to farming, not that he dispatched envoys.

proposals.before: "By what bright decree do you carry out making wealthy families issue grain?"
proposals.after: "By what explicit official order are you making wealthy families issue grain?"
proposals.reason: 明令 is an explicit official order, not a 'bright' decree; the literal calque obscures the official-command sense.

proposals.before: Costs float and lands are distant, partners grab the profit—two;
proposals.after: High costs and distant territories let partners grab the profit—two;
proposals.reason: 費浮 means inflated or excessive costs, not that costs 'float'.

proposals.before: When someone reported that a certain family was not selling grain, he had him beaten with the bamboo and said;
proposals.after: When someone reported that a certain family was not selling grain, he had him beaten with the bamboo and said:
proposals.reason: The Chinese colon/semicolon before the quotation is rendered as a sentence-final semicolon, which breaks the speech frame continued in the next unit.

proposals.before: During the Qianlong reign he entered service through hereditary privilege as assistant prefect at Nanhe, Shan, and Huai.
proposals.after: During the Qianlong reign he entered service through hereditary privilege as assistant prefect of Shanxu under the Southern River administration.
proposals.reason: 南河山盱通判 is the Shanxu assistant prefecture in the Southern River conservancy, not three places called Nanhe, Shan, and Huai.

proposals.before: During Qianlong, by hereditary privilege he was appointed assistant prefect of Nanhe, Shan, and Huai.
proposals.after: During Qianlong, by hereditary privilege he was appointed assistant prefect of Shanxu in the Southern River administration.
proposals.reason: The literal rendering splits 山盱 into Shan and Huai; 山盱 is the river-works office name Shanxu.

proposals.before: Xi Di said: "Your victory through unexpected stratagem lay in the support dike you built in advance beforehand."
proposals.after: Xidi said: "Your victory through unexpected stratagem lay in the support dike you built in advance beforehand."
proposals.reason: 錫第 is the given name Xidi of Lan Xidi, not a two-word name Xi Di.

proposals.before: Early in the Yongzheng reign he was nominated as a Filial and Incorrupt scholar and appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Works.
proposals.after: Early in the Yongzheng reign, as a government student, he was nominated as Filial, Incorrupt, and Upright and appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Works.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 諸生 and shortens 孝廉方正 to Filial and Incorrupt, dropping 方正 (Upright).

proposals.before: He was soon demoted over a political dispute.
proposals.after: He was soon demoted over an affair.
proposals.reason: 以事 is an unspecified matter; calling it a political dispute invents a cause the Chinese does not state.

proposals.before: Governor Hu Baoheng exclaimed with delight, "The state has gained an excellent Director-General of Rivers!"
proposals.after: Governor Hu Baoheng exclaimed with delight, "I have obtained for the state an excellent Director-General of Rivers!"
proposals.reason: The quotation begins 吾為國家得, first-person I obtained for the state, which the idiomatic rendering drops.

decisions.reason: Chinese 擢沁州知州，署潞安知府 promotes him as department magistrate (知州) of Qinzhou and only then as acting prefect (署…知府) of Lu'an; the original English makes both prefectures and adds concurrent service that 署 does not state.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 擢沁州知州，署潞安知府

decisions.reason: The literal English likewise renders 沁州知州 as prefect, colliding with the distinct 知府 of 潞安; department magistrate of Qinzhou is the accurate office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 擢沁州知州，署潞安知府

decisions.reason: 僧了凡等四人 names the monk Liaofan among four people; plural 'monks' wrongly makes the three others monks as well.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 蕭山捕僧了凡等四人

decisions.reason: 素無籍 means he had long lacked household registration (籍), not that he lacked a fixed occupation.

decisions.after: Xi was ordered to join in the joint investigation. He determined guilt and innocence justly throughout and released Wenjia and all those implicated with him. Fugitives returned from hiding, and the border was pacified.
decisions.reason: 蔽罪悉當 means the assignments of guilt were all fitting, so the original 'charges groundless throughout' is the reverse of the Chinese; the proposed wording is right in sense but needs 'and' before 'released'.
